answer: Resource-testing makes sybils expensive: each new agent must pass a timed task whose hidden inputs are drawn after registration, like a mirror held up to its real compute. Honest agents solve one task each; an attacker with 1,000 fake identities must fund 1,000 simultaneous solves, so cost scales linearly. Results are signed with a quill-style commitment, and a summit of random auditors re-checks samples, slashing proven duplicates.
